To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pathways core data model can: * be implemented on top of existing data models used by repositories, * provide a common data model for cross repository services, * provide a lightweight, simple, and flexible framework for representing compound objects, and * be used as a shared data profile for repositories, services, and applications.
The pathways core data model has been designed to be lightweight and to be widely usable as a shared profile.
(1) The pathways data model is designed as a profile of the Dublin Core metadata standard, which is itself a profile of the ISO-2789 standard for library cataloguing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a core data model for the representation of objects in digital repositories and the implementation of a set of cross-repository web services that can be built upon this model.

developing a common data model for digital repositories, which will enable the creation of a set of cross-repository tools and services that can be used to enhance the functionality and interoperability of repositories.

(1) identifying the common data elements and structures required to support the full range of cross-repository applications, and (2) developing a model that is lightweight to implement, yet flexible and expressive enough to support a wide variety of data models and applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single best way to represent compound objects.

the pathways core data model provides an interoperable data format for the representation of digital objects, with a focus on compound objects, that can be used as a common profile, or as an overlay to existing data models, to facilitate cross-repository services.
the pathways core data model can serve as a common profile for interoperability between repository systems and as a basis for the development of cross-repository applications and services.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have created an abstract model that can be mapped onto a number of existing models, and can be used to support a broad spectrum of services.
we have designed a data model to support the creation of cross-repository applications, such as the creation of compound objects and services for compound objects.
we have created a data model that is both lightweight and widely applicable, and that can be implemented with minimal effort.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a shared data model for compound objects, such as the pathways core model, can be used to facilitate the creation and re-use of digital objects across repositories.
the core data model is not a panacea, but rather it provides a useful starting point for a number of cross-repository applications.

a common data model can be constructed that is sufficiently general to accommodate a wide variety of repository implementations and data formats, and that is sufficiently specific to enable interoperability and re-use of objects across repository systems.
